samples.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small ladder: four thin vertical rails of the same length standing side by side, joined by short horizontal rungs. Each rung joins two neighbouring rails, and every rung sits at its own height, so no two rungs are level. A small coloured square is welded under the bottom end of each rail; the four squares are red, green, blue and purple in some order. A solid dark triangular tab sits just above the top end of exactly one rail, and that rail is where the walk begins. The walk moves downwards. Whenever it reaches an end of a rung on the rail it is currently on, it crosses that rung to the neighbouring rail and then carries on downwards from there; rungs are met in top-to-bottom order, and a rung that does not touch the rail the walk is currently on is passed by with no effect. The walk ends at the bottom end of whichever rail it is on then. The ladder may sit anywhere on the canvas, and every grey mark outside the ladder is inert decoration. Which colour is the square under the rail where the walk ends? Answer with one of red, green, blue or purple.
